title: Trivia
source: Written for Henry (Nov 25) for his Club: 500 trivia questions for ages 12-15 in 5 sets of 100 (General Knowledge, Dictionary, History, Geography, Science & Nature). About 50% regular, 35% hard, 15% impossible; roughly 20% Thailand and Asia. Every question has a tier and a one-line why. American English. Written from memory: skim the hard ones before relying on them.

questions.q: What is the Japanese art of folding paper called?
questions.why: "Ori" means folding and "kami" means paper.

questions.q: Which painter cut off part of his own ear?
questions.why: He painted "The Starry Night".

questions.q: What is a group of fish called?
questions.why: Fish swim together in schools.

questions.q: Which Thai martial art is called the "art of eight limbs"?
questions.why: It uses fists, elbows, knees and shins.

questions.q: What is the name of the three-wheeled taxi often seen in Thailand?
questions.why: Its name copies the sound of its engine.

questions.q: In chess, which piece moves only diagonally?
questions.why: The bishop stays on one color of squares.

questions.q: Which sport uses a ball called a "puck"?
questions.why: A puck is a flat rubber disc.

questions.q: Which Thai ancient capital is a UNESCO World Heritage site north of Bangkok, with many ruined temples?
questions.why: Ayutthaya was the capital for about 400 years.

questions.q: How many players from one team are on a basketball court at the same time?
questions.why: Five players per team play at once.

questions.q: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
questions.why: It was a gift in 1886.

questions.q: In which sport can you win the "Green Jacket"?
questions.why: It is given to the winner of the Masters.

questions.q: What is the main language spoken in Brazil?
questions.why: Brazil was once a Portuguese colony.

questions.q: What is the national animal of Thailand?
questions.why: The Thai elephant is the national animal.

questions.q: How many time zones does Russia have?
questions.why: Russia is the largest country and stretches across 11 time zones.

questions.q: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cups?
questions.why: Brazil has won five times.

questions.q: Which country is the origin of the martial art taekwondo?
questions.why: Taekwondo means "the way of the foot and fist".

questions.q: Which sport is played at Wimbledon?
questions.why: Wimbledon is a famous tennis tournament in London.

questions.q: Which popular video game is a block-building sandbox game made by Mojang?
questions.why: Mojang was bought by Microsoft in 2014.

questions.q: What is the Japanese word for a traditional robe?
questions.why: The Korean one is hanbok.

questions.q: Which river flows through Bangkok?
questions.why: The Chao Phraya flows into the Gulf of Thailand.

questions.q: In which sport might you do a "slam dunk"?
questions.why: You jump and put the ball down through the hoop.

questions.q: Which famous Thai landmark in Bangkok is also called the Temple of the Emerald Buddha?
questions.why: It stands inside the Grand Palace.

questions.q: In which sport do you score a "touchdown"?
questions.why: A touchdown is worth six points.

questions.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.why: Two pump blood to the gills and one to the body.

questions.q: Which Thai festival has people float small decorated baskets on the water?
questions.why: Loy Krathong is held on the full moon of the 12th lunar month.

questions.q: How many points is the letter Q worth in English Scrabble?
questions.why: Q and Z are worth 10 points.

questions.q: What does the Japanese word "karaoke" mean?
questions.why: Kara means empty and oke is short for orchestra.

questions.q: What are the three primary colors of light?
questions.why: Screens mix red, green and blue light.

questions.q: In music, how many beats does a whole note usually get in 4/4 time?
questions.why: A whole note lasts four beats.

questions.q: Which country first used paper money?
questions.why: Paper money appeared in China about 1,000 years ago.

questions.q: What is the name for a baby swan?
questions.why: A cygnet is a young swan.

questions.q: Which sport uses the terms "love", "deuce" and "advantage"?
questions.why: These are tennis scoring words.

questions.q: Which superhero is also known as the Caped Crusader?
questions.why: Batman lives in Gotham City.

questions.q: Which animal is the symbol of the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF)?
questions.why: The panda logo is black and white.

questions.q: Which Thai city is famous for the Yi Peng lantern festival?
questions.why: Thousands of lanterns are released into the sky.

questions.q: Which is the largest coral reef system in the world?
questions.why: It is off the coast of Australia and more than 2,000 km long.

questions.q: Which sport uses a shuttlecock?
questions.why: A shuttlecock has feathers or plastic skirts.

questions.q: Which Thai fruit is called the "king of fruits" because of its strong smell?
questions.why: The mangosteen is called the "queen".

questions.q: Which Thai dessert is made from mango and sticky rice?
questions.why: The rice is cooked in coconut milk.

questions.q: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.why: They stand for five regions of the world.

questions.q: What kind of animal is Simba in "The Lion King"?
questions.why: Simba is a lion cub.

questions.q: Which Tolstoy novel is about Russia during the wars with Napoleon?
questions.why: It is more than 1,200 pages long.

questions.q: How many players are there on a volleyball team on the court?
questions.why: Six players per team are on the court.

questions.q: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
questions.why: Most guitars have six strings.

questions.q: What is the pre-fight dance of Muay Thai called?
questions.why: Fighters honor their teachers with it.

questions.q: Which king founded Bangkok as the capital in 1782?
questions.why: Rama I started the Chakri dynasty.

questions.q: How many continents are there?
questions.why: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia/Oceania.

questions.q: Which Thai dish's name means "papaya salad"?
questions.why: Som tam is made with shredded green papaya.

questions.q: In which sport do players try to score a "birdie"?
questions.why: A birdie is one stroke under par.

questions.q: Which food is Japan famous for, made with vinegared rice and often raw fish?
questions.why: Sushi comes from Japan.

questions.q: How many keys are on a standard modern piano?
questions.why: There are 52 white and 36 black keys.

questions.q: What is the term for a story that is not real and is written for children, with a moral?
questions.why: Aesop wrote many fables.

questions.q: What do you get when you mix blue and yellow paint?
questions.why: Blue and yellow make green.

questions.q: What is the national sport of Japan, in which two wrestlers push each other out of a ring?
questions.why: Sumo is hundreds of years old.

questions.q: How many sides does a stop sign have?
questions.why: A stop sign is an octagon.

questions.q: Who composed the music for "Swan Lake"?
questions.why: He also composed "The Nutcracker".

questions.q: Which sport is often called "the beautiful game"?
questions.why: Pelé made this nickname famous.

questions.q: What is the most spoken first language in the world?
questions.why: More people speak Mandarin as a first language than any other language.

questions.q: What color is the hat of the video game character Mario?
questions.why: His brother Luigi wears green.

questions.q: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.why: Japan uses the yen.

questions.q: Which sport has a score called "love"?
questions.why: Love means zero in tennis.

questions.q: What is the main ingredient of bread?
questions.why: Bread dough is flour, water and yeast.

questions.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
questions.why: A leap year adds February 29.

questions.q: Which country is known as the "Land of the Rising Sun"?
questions.why: The name comes from Japan's position in the east.

questions.q: In what year did the first iPhone go on sale?
questions.why: Steve Jobs announced it in January 2007.

questions.q: What is the name of the famous Thai dish made with stir-fried rice noodles, egg and peanuts?
questions.why: Pad Thai is stir-fried noodles.

questions.q: Which country is famous for the Eiffel Tower?
questions.why: The tower stands in Paris.

questions.q: What is the name of the wizard school in the Harry Potter books?
questions.why: Harry studies at Hogwarts.

questions.q: What is the name of the Italian city with canals and gondolas?
questions.why: Venice is built on more than 100 small islands.

questions.q: Which composer wrote "The Four Seasons"?
questions.why: Vivaldi was Italian.

questions.q: What is the name for the 50th birthday or 50th anniversary?
questions.why: Fifty years is golden; 25 is silver.

questions.q: In which sport is the Ryder Cup played?
questions.why: Teams from Europe and the USA play for it.

questions.q: What is the name of the popular Thai soup with lemongrass, lime leaves and shrimp?
questions.why: Tom Yum Goong is hot and sour.

questions.q: Which Olympic sport uses a vault, a balance beam and uneven bars?
questions.why: These are gymnastics apparatus.

questions.q: What is the color of the middle stripe on the Thai flag?
questions.why: The Thai flag is red, white, blue, white, red.

questions.q: Which country is the home of the sport of golf?
questions.why: Golf was played in Scotland in the 1400s.

questions.q: Which Thai king is remembered for an elephant duel against a Burmese prince in 1593?
questions.why: He freed Ayutthaya from Burmese rule.

questions.q: What is the Roman numeral for 50?
questions.why: C is 100, D is 500 and X is 10.

questions.q: Which animal gives us wool?
questions.why: Sheep are shorn for their wool.

questions.q: What do you call a baby kangaroo?
questions.why: A joey grows in its mother's pouch.

questions.q: Which board game has the pieces king, queen, rook, bishop, knight and pawn?
questions.why: Chess has six kinds of pieces.

questions.q: Which cartoon character lives in a pineapple under the sea?
questions.why: His home is in Bikini Bottom.

questions.q: Which Northern Thai dance is performed with long golden fingernails?
questions.why: Dancers wear long, curved nail covers.

questions.q: What is Songkran?
choices: The Thai New Year water festival
questions.why: Songkran is in April, and people splash water.

questions.q: What is the tallest animal in the world?
questions.why: A giraffe can be about 5 meters tall.

questions.q: Which author created the detective Sherlock Holmes?
questions.why: Holmes lived at 221B Baker Street.

questions.q: What does a "hat-trick" mean in soccer?
choices: Winning three games in a row
questions.why: A player scores three goals in one game.

questions.q: How many colors are in a rainbow?
questions.why: Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

questions.q: Which country is called the "Land of Fire and Ice"?
questions.why: Iceland has both volcanoes and glaciers.

questions.q: Which instrument has black and white keys?
questions.why: A piano has 88 keys.

questions.q: What is the term for a word that is spelled the same forward and backward, like "level"?
questions.why: Racecar is another palindrome.

questions.q: Who wrote "Romeo and Juliet"?
questions.why: Shakespeare wrote it in the 1590s.

questions.q: Which musical instrument has a bow and four strings and is played under the chin?
questions.why: The violin is the smallest string instrument in an orchestra.

questions.q: In what year were the modern Olympic Games first held in Athens?
questions.why: Pierre de Coubertin helped revive the Games.

questions.q: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.why: Leonardo painted it in the early 1500s.

questions.q: Which artist painted "The Persistence of Memory" with melting clocks?
questions.why: Dali was a Spanish surrealist.

questions.q: What does "WWW" stand for in a web address?
questions.why: It is the system of pages linked on the internet.

questions.q: What is the name of the Japanese poem form with three lines of 5, 7 and 5 syllables?
questions.why: A haiku often describes nature.

questions.q: How many consonants are in the Thai alphabet?
questions.why: Thai also has about 15 vowel symbols.

questions.q: Which company makes the iPhone?
questions.why: Apple released the first iPhone in 2007.

questions.q: What is the opposite of "arrive"?
questions.why: Depart means to leave.

questions.q: Which word means "a person who lives next to you"?
questions.why: Neighbors live close to your home.

questions.q: Which word means "to jump quickly into the air"?
questions.why: A frog can leap far.

questions.q: What does "delicious" mean?
questions.why: Delicious food tastes great.

questions.q: What does "ambiguous" mean?
choices: Having more than one possible meaning
questions.why: An ambiguous answer can be understood in two ways.

questions.q: What is "onomatopoeia"?
choices: A word with a hidden meaning
A word that sounds like the thing it names
A word that has no vowels
questions.why: "Buzz" and "splash" are examples.

questions.q: What does "bilingual" mean?
questions.why: Bi- means two.

questions.q: What is the plural of "mouse" (the animal)?
questions.why: Mice is an irregular plural.

questions.q: What is a "monarch"?
questions.why: A monarch rules a country.

questions.q: Which of these is a synonym of "big"?
questions.why: Large and big mean the same.

questions.q: What does the word "nocturnal" mean?
questions.why: Owls are nocturnal animals.

questions.q: What does "sycophant" mean?
choices: A person who flatters powerful people to get ahead
questions.why: The word comes from Greek.

questions.q: What does the word "quintessential" mean?
questions.why: Pad Thai is a quintessential Thai dish.

questions.q: What is the difference between "affect" and "effect"?
choices: Affect is usually a verb; effect is usually a noun
questions.why: Weather can affect your mood; it has an effect.

questions.q: Which is the correct spelling?
questions.why: It has a double R and a double S.

questions.q: Which word means "a very small piece of something"?
questions.why: A crumb of bread.

questions.q: What does "serendipity" mean?
choices: Finding something good by lucky accident
questions.why: Penicillin is often called a serendipitous discovery.

questions.q: What does "journey" mean?
questions.why: A journey is travel from one place to another.

questions.q: What does "dilemma" mean?
choices: A difficult choice between two options
questions.why: A dilemma has no easy answer.

questions.q: What does the prefix "re-" mean in "rewrite"?
questions.why: Rewrite means write again.

questions.q: What is the opposite of "expensive"?
questions.why: Cheap things cost little.

questions.q: What is the noun form of "decide"?
questions.why: Decide becomes decision.

questions.q: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.why: It means your sense of right and wrong.

questions.q: What does "ambivalent" mean?
questions.why: You like and dislike something at once.

questions.q: What does "vivid" mean?
questions.why: A vivid color or memory is strong and clear.

questions.q: What is a synonym of "happy"?
questions.why: Cheerful means happy and bright.

questions.q: Which word means "to make something less severe"?
questions.why: You can alleviate pain.

questions.q: What does the idiom "under the weather" mean?
questions.why: It describes a mild illness.

questions.q: Which word means "to show that something is true"?
questions.why: Scientists prove ideas with evidence.

questions.q: What does "obsequious" mean?
choices: Too eager to please or obey
questions.why: An obsequious person flatters everyone.

questions.q: What does "exhausted" mean?
questions.why: You feel exhausted after a long run.

questions.q: What does "obsolete" mean?
choices: No longer used because something newer exists
questions.why: A typewriter is obsolete for most people.

questions.q: Which word means "to look at something quickly"?
questions.why: A glance is a short look.

questions.q: What is the meaning of "ephemeral"?
questions.why: A rainbow is ephemeral.

questions.q: Which word means "a place where you borrow books"?
questions.why: You borrow books free at a library.

questions.q: What does "fluent" mean when we talk about a language?
choices: Able to speak easily and well
questions.why: A fluent speaker does not stop and search for words.

questions.q: What do we call a word that has the same meaning as another word?
questions.why: Big and large are synonyms.

questions.q: Which of these words is an adjective?
questions.why: Colorful describes a noun.

questions.q: What is the opposite of "ancient"?
questions.why: Ancient things are very old; modern things are new.

questions.q: Which of these words is a verb?
questions.why: Jump describes an action.

questions.q: What does the idiom "the elephant in the room" mean?
choices: An obvious problem nobody wants to talk about
questions.why: People avoid the topic.

questions.q: What does "repair" mean?
questions.why: You repair a broken bike.

questions.q: Which word is the opposite of "difficult"?
questions.why: Easy and difficult are opposites.

questions.q: Which word sounds the same as "knight"?
questions.why: Knight and night are homophones.

questions.q: What does "enormous" mean?
questions.why: Enormous means extremely large.

questions.q: What is the opposite of "brave"?
questions.why: A cowardly person is afraid of danger.

questions.q: Which word means "to get information from many different places and put it together"?
questions.why: Writers compile lists and reports.

questions.q: What does "reluctant" mean?
questions.why: A reluctant student does not want to speak.

questions.q: Which is the correct spelling?
questions.why: Double C and double M.

questions.q: Which word is a synonym of "begin"?
questions.why: Begin and start mean the same.

questions.q: What does "juxtapose" mean?
choices: To place two things side by side to compare
questions.why: Artists juxtapose light and dark.

questions.q: What does the idiom "hit the books" mean?
questions.why: Students hit the books before exams.

questions.q: Which is the correct spelling?
questions.why: Definitely has "finite" inside it.

questions.q: What is a synonym of "meticulous"?
questions.why: A meticulous person pays attention to every detail.

questions.q: Which word means "to give food or drink to someone"?
questions.why: Farmers feed their animals.

questions.q: What does "brave" mean?
questions.why: A brave person faces danger.

questions.q: What does "hypothesis" mean?
choices: An idea that can be tested
questions.why: Scientists test a hypothesis.

questions.q: What does "ostentatious" mean?
choices: Showing off wealth in a way meant to impress
questions.why: An ostentatious house is too showy.

questions.q: What is a "pet"?
questions.why: Dogs and cats are common pets.

questions.q: Which word means "happening every year"?
questions.why: Annual comes from the Latin word for year.

questions.q: What does the suffix "-ful" mean in "helpful"?
questions.why: Helpful means full of help.

questions.q: What does "benevolent" mean?
questions.why: Bene means "good" in Latin.

questions.q: Which word describes a person who does not like to waste anything?
questions.why: Thrifty and frugal are close in meaning.

questions.q: What does the prefix "un-" do in "unhappy"?
questions.why: Unhappy means not happy.

questions.q: What does "pragmatic" mean?
choices: Dealing with things in a practical way
questions.why: A pragmatic person is sensible and realistic.

questions.q: What does the suffix "-less" mean in "careless"?
questions.why: Careless means without care.

questions.q: What is an "oxymoron"?
choices: Two words with opposite meanings used together
questions.why: "Deafening silence" is an oxymoron.

questions.q: What is the opposite of "scarce"?
questions.why: Scarce means hard to find.

questions.q: What does "borrow" mean?
choices: To take something and give it back later
questions.why: You borrow a book from the library.

questions.q: Which word sounds the same as "write" but is spelled differently?
questions.why: Write and right are homophones.

questions.q: What does "inevitable" mean?
questions.why: It cannot be avoided.

questions.q: What does "frugal" mean?
questions.why: A frugal person does not waste money.

questions.q: What does "silent" mean?
questions.why: A silent room is completely quiet.

questions.q: What is a "dictionary"?
choices: A book that explains the meanings of words
questions.why: You can look words up in it.

questions.q: What does the idiom "a piece of cake" mean?
questions.why: The test was a piece of cake.

questions.q: What is the adjective form of "danger"?
questions.why: Dangerous means likely to cause harm.

questions.q: Which word means "to make something better"?
questions.why: You improve by practicing.

questions.q: What is a "palindrome"?
choices: A word that reads the same forward and backward
questions.why: "Madam" and "level" are palindromes.

questions.q: What does "magnanimous" mean?
choices: Generous and forgiving, especially to a rival
questions.why: A magnanimous winner is kind to the loser.

questions.q: Which word means "very, very hungry"?
questions.why: Starving can mean extremely hungry.

questions.q: Which word means "to say sorry"?
questions.why: You apologize when you are sorry.

questions.q: Which word means "to talk about something with others before deciding"?
questions.why: Classmates discuss a problem together.

questions.q: What does "curious" mean?
choices: Wanting to know or learn more
questions.why: Curious children ask many questions.

questions.q: What is the plural of "child"?
questions.why: Child has an irregular plural.

questions.q: What does "persuade" mean?
choices: To make someone agree to do something
questions.why: You persuade with good reasons.

questions.q: Which word means "money you earn from work"?
questions.why: A salary is regular pay.

questions.q: What is a "euphemism"?
choices: A mild word used instead of a harsh one
questions.why: "Passed away" is a euphemism for "died".

questions.q: What does the idiom "spill the beans" mean?
questions.why: You reveal something that was hidden.

questions.q: What do we call a word that means the opposite of another word?
questions.why: Hot and cold are antonyms.

questions.q: Which word sounds the same as "sea"?
questions.why: Sea and see are homophones.

questions.q: Which is the correct spelling?
questions.why: Remember: "a rat" in sepARATe.

questions.q: Which word sounds the same as "two"?
questions.why: Two, to and too sound the same.

questions.q: What does "drizzle" mean?
questions.why: A drizzle is gentle, fine rain.

questions.q: What does "ubiquitous" mean?
questions.why: Smartphones are ubiquitous.

questions.q: What is the opposite of "generous"?
questions.why: A generous person gives freely.

questions.q: What does the idiom "break the ice" mean?
questions.why: It helps people feel comfortable.

questions.q: Which word means "a short sleep during the day"?
questions.why: A nap is a short sleep.

questions.q: What does an "acronym" do?
choices: Changes a verb to a noun
Makes a word from the first letters of other words
questions.why: NASA stands for National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

questions.q: Which of these words is an adverb?
questions.why: Carefully describes how you do something.

questions.q: Which is the correct spelling?
questions.why: One C and two S: necessary.

questions.q: What was the Silk Road?
choices: A network of trade routes linking China and Europe
questions.why: Silk, spices and ideas traveled along it.

questions.q: Which year did the Chinese Communist Party win and Mao Zedong declare the People's Republic of China?
questions.why: He announced it in Beijing.

questions.q: Which ancient civilization built the pyramids at Giza?
questions.why: The Great Pyramid was built about 4,500 years ago.

questions.q: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin?
questions.why: Factories and steam engines grew there in the 1700s.

questions.q: Which ship sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg?
questions.why: It was on its first trip from England to New York.

questions.q: Which ancient wonder was a huge tomb built for a pharaoh in Egypt?
questions.why: It is the only ancient wonder still standing.

questions.q: Which old Thai capital has a Buddha head wrapped in tree roots?
questions.why: It is at Wat Mahathat in Ayutthaya.

questions.q: What was the old name of Thailand before 1939?
questions.why: The country changed its name to Thailand in 1939.

questions.q: In which country did the Renaissance begin?
questions.why: It started in Florence in the 1300s.

questions.q: Which ancient Greek thinker was the teacher of Alexander the Great?
questions.why: Aristotle was a student of Plato.

questions.q: In what year did the Black Death reach Europe, killing about a third of its people?
questions.why: It arrived by ships from the Black Sea.

questions.q: In which year did World War II end?
questions.why: The war ended in 1945.

questions.q: Who founded the Tokugawa shogunate, which ruled Japan for over 250 years?
questions.why: The shogunate lasted from 1603 to 1868.

questions.q: What was the Berlin Wall?
choices: A wall that divided a city in Germany
questions.why: It stood from 1961 to 1989.

questions.q: Who invented the telephone?
questions.why: He made the first call in 1876.

questions.q: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.why: Washington led the country from 1789 to 1797.

questions.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.why: He stepped out in July 1969.

questions.q: Which empire was ruled by Julius Caesar and Augustus?
questions.why: Rome was once the capital of a huge empire.

questions.q: Which king signed the Magna Carta in 1215?
questions.why: It limited the king's power.

questions.q: Who was known as the "Iron Lady" and was Britain's first woman prime minister?
questions.why: She served from 1979 to 1990.

questions.q: Which Thai king signed the Bowring Treaty with Britain in 1855?
questions.why: Mongkut opened Siam to trade with the West.

questions.q: What was the name of the sickness that killed millions in Europe in the 1300s?
questions.why: It spread by fleas on rats.

questions.q: What event started on September 1, 1939 in Europe?
questions.why: Germany invaded Poland.

questions.q: Which wall was built in ancient China to keep invaders out?
questions.why: Parts of it are more than 2,000 years old.

questions.q: Who was the Soviet leader during most of World War II?
questions.why: He led the USSR from the 1920s to 1953.

questions.q: What invention by Johannes Gutenberg changed Europe in the 1400s?
questions.why: Books became much cheaper.

questions.q: Which Mongol leader founded the Yuan dynasty in China?
questions.why: He was Genghis Khan's grandson.

questions.q: Which ancient wonder was in the city of Babylon and had terraces of plants?
questions.why: Historians are not sure where exactly it was.

questions.q: In which battle was Napoleon finally defeated in 1815?
questions.why: Waterloo is in present-day Belgium.

questions.q: Which event began in 1914 and is often called "the Great War"?
questions.why: It lasted from 1914 to 1918.

questions.q: Who was the last ruling emperor of China (Qing dynasty) who gave up the throne in 1912?
questions.why: He became emperor as a small child.

questions.q: Which Italian explorer traveled to China in the 1200s and wrote about it?
questions.why: His book was "The Travels of Marco Polo".

questions.q: Which scientist developed the theory of relativity?
questions.why: E = mc² is his famous equation.

questions.q: Which famous French leader became emperor in 1804?
questions.why: He crowned himself emperor.

questions.q: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
questions.why: He painted it between 1508 and 1512.

questions.q: In which year was the American Declaration of Independence adopted?
questions.why: It was adopted on July 4, 1776.

questions.q: Which South African leader spent 27 years in prison and later became president?
questions.why: He became president in 1994.

questions.q: What is the name of the Thai city that was the first capital of the Thai kingdom in the 1200s?
questions.why: Sukhothai means "dawn of happiness".

questions.q: What was the name of the first successful English colony in North America, founded in 1607?
questions.why: It is in present-day Virginia.

questions.q: What did the Rosetta Stone help scholars read?
questions.why: It had the same text in three scripts.

questions.q: What kind of animal is a frog?
questions.why: Amphibians live in water and on land.

questions.q: Which scientist discovered radioactivity in uranium in 1896?
questions.why: Marie Curie later named it "radioactivity".

questions.q: What do we call a scientist who studies animals?
questions.why: Zoo- comes from the Greek word for animal.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.why: Iron oxide (rust) gives Mars its red color.
